figures.name: Mor Aphrem (Ephrem the Syrian)
figures.description: Theologian, poet, and hymnographer. Wrote extensively in Syriac and is considered one of the greatest Aramean literary figures.

figures.name: Mor Yaqub of Serugh
figures.description: Prolific Syriac poet and bishop, known for his metrical homilies. Wrote over 760 verse homilies in Syriac.

figures.name: Bar Hebraeus (Mor Gregorios Abu al-Faraj)
figures.description: Maphrian of the Syriac Orthodox Church, polymath, historian, and theologian. Wrote in Syriac and Arabic on theology, philosophy, grammar, and history.

figures.name: Hazael
figures.description: King of Aram-Damascus who expanded the kingdom to its greatest territorial extent, defeating Israel and Judah.

figures.name: Abgar V Ukama
figures.description: Aramean king of Osroene (Edessa/Urhoy). According to tradition, corresponded with Jesus and was healed by the Apostle Thaddeus.

figures.name: Mor Michael Rabo (Michael the Great)
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and author of the largest surviving Syriac historical work, the Chronicle.

figures.name: Nabopolassar
figures.description: Chaldean (Kaldu-Aramean) general who founded the Neo-Babylonian Empire and destroyed the Assyrian Empire.

figures.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
figures.description: King of the Neo-Babylonian (Chaldean) Empire. Built the Hanging Gardens and expanded the empire to its greatest extent.

figures.name: Mor Yaqub Burd'ono (Jacob Baradaeus)
figures.description: Bishop who revived the Syriac Orthodox Church by secretly ordaining clergy across the region. The church was sometimes called 'Jacobite' after him.

figures.name: Bardaisan (Bar Daysan)
figures.description: Philosopher, scientist, and poet from Edessa. One of the earliest Syriac writers, known for his hymns and cosmological works.

figures.name: Tatian the Assyrian
figures.description: Aramean theologian who composed the Diatessaron, a harmony of the four Gospels in Syriac that was widely used in the Syriac-speaking church.

figures.name: Zenobia
figures.description: Queen of the Palmyrene Empire who briefly conquered Egypt and much of the Roman East. Ruled from the Aramean city of Palmyra.

figures.name: Mor Aphrem Barsoum
figures.description: Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch and scholar. Authored 'The Scattered Pearls', a history of Syriac literature and sciences.

figures.name: Naim Faiq
figures.description: Aramean journalist and activist who advocated for Aramean national identity. Published the newspaper 'Kawkab Madnho' (Star of the East).

figures.name: Lucian of Samosata
figures.description: Satirist and rhetorician from Samosata (Commagene). Wrote in Greek but identified himself as an Aramean ('Syrian barbarian').

figures.name: Hezion
figures.description: Founder of the Aram-Damascus dynasty (biblical).

figures.name: Tabrimmon
figures.description: Son of Hezion, king of Aram-Damascus.

figures.name: Ben-Hadad I
figures.description: King of Aram-Damascus who allied with Asa of Judah against Israel.

figures.name: Hadadezer
figures.description: King of Aram-Damascus who led the anti-Assyrian coalition at the Battle of Qarqar (853 BC).

figures.name: Ben-Hadad III
figures.description: Son of Hazael. Under his reign, Aram-Damascus declined in power.

figures.name: Rezin
figures.description: Last king of Aram-Damascus. Conquered by Tiglath-Pileser III in 732 BC.

figures.name: Hadadezer of Zobah
figures.description: King of Aram-Zobah, defeated by David of Israel (2 Samuel 8).

figures.name: Talmai
figures.description: King of Geshur and father-in-law of David (2 Samuel 3:3).

figures.name: Toi (Tou)
figures.description: King of Hamath, contemporary of David. Sent gifts after the defeat of Hadadezer of Zobah.

figures.name: Irhuleni
figures.description: King of Hamath who fought against Assyria at the Battle of Qarqar.

figures.name: Zakkur
figures.description: King of Hamath and Lu'ash. Erected the Zakkur Stele commemorating his victory over a coalition led by Bar-Hadad.

figures.name: Gusi
figures.description: Founder of the Bit-Agusi dynasty.

figures.name: Arame
figures.description: Second king of Bit-Agusi who submitted to Assyria.

figures.name: Attarsumki
figures.description: King of Bit-Agusi, vassal of Adad-nirari III.

figures.name: Mati'el
figures.description: Last independent king of Bit-Agusi. Party to the Sefire treaties. Defeated by Tiglath-Pileser III after a three-year siege.

figures.name: Ahuni
figures.description: Last king of Bit-Adini. Defeated and deported by Shalmaneser III.

figures.name: Gabbar
figures.description: Founder of the Bit-Gabbar dynasty at Sam'al.

figures.name: Kilamuwa
figures.description: King of Bit-Gabbar who erected the Kilamuwa Stele.

figures.name: Panamuwa I
figures.description: King of Bit-Gabbar who erected the Hadad statue inscription in Samalian Aramaic.

figures.name: Bar-Sur
figures.description: Usurper who seized the throne of Bit-Gabbar.

figures.name: Panamuwa II
figures.description: Restored to the throne by Tiglath-Pileser III. Died during the Assyrian campaign against Damascus.

figures.name: Bar-Rakib
figures.description: Last king of Bit-Gabbar. Loyal Assyrian vassal who left multiple inscriptions.

figures.name: Kapara
figures.description: Ruler of Bit-Bahiani who built the famous palace at Tell Halaf (Guzana).

figures.name: Merodach-Baladan II
figures.description: Chaldean/Aramean leader who twice seized the throne of Babylon and allied with Elam against Assyria.
